# DatePicker

A date field that can be typed or picked from a calendar.

```tsx
import { DatePicker } from '@kafka-ds/react'
```

## When to use it

- Whenever a date is needed.

## When not to

- For a date range: use two fields.

## Examples

### Typed or picked

Both ways write the same value (`YYYY-MM-DD`). The calendar opens in a popover and returns focus to its button.

```tsx
<Demo />
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | `string \| null` |  | The date as `YYYY-MM-DD`, or `null` when empty. |
| `onValueChange` | `(iso: string \| null) => void` |  |  |
| `order` | `'dmy' \| 'mdy' \| 'ymd'` | `'dmy'` | Order of day, month and year when typing: `dmy` (31/12/2026), `mdy` or `ymd`. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `id` | `string` |  |  |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |
| …rest | `Pick<CalendarProps, 'min' \| 'max' \| 'locale' \| 'weekStartsOn'>` | | Everything else is passed to the underlying element. |

## Accessibility

- The field accepts typing in day/month/year order and validates on blur; the calendar button opens a Popover.
- The button has its own name ("Abrir calendario"); choosing a day closes it and returns focus to the button.
- Put it inside a Field so it has a label, hint and error.

## Content

- Tell the reader the expected format in the hint.
